title: A decision without Dinis: Web Summit's terms read, and every automated read of its site stopped in under two minutes
summary: At 05:26:18 incident.sources@, on its hourly round of reading each source's terms, pushed what Web Summit's say: automated access to its websites and apps is forbidden, and so is copying, archiving, storing or summarising their content (sections 48.2 and 52.1, as that agent read them).
This site had polled the organiser's blog every two minutes, captured its pages, and ten timeline rows link to it. The agent stopped its own requests and put the choice to Dinis as an ask.

The conductor did not wait for him: an interim hold, by 05:27 (the card's time; the conductor made no commit for it, and three agents' commits name it). Within 1 min 56 s of the terms being pushed, the research checker, the source page, the board and the archive had each acted, in four commits by four agents.

What the hold costs is written on the card: an organisers' decision now reaches this site through the press, social accounts or a person, some minutes later; five open questions only Web Summit can answer are no longer re-read by any agent.

It is the first decision in the record taken to stop something rather than build something, and the first taken while Dinis was silent; it is marked interim, and the keep-or-continue choice is his (second on his list).
